item.subject: maths
item.stem:
Meher looks at the diagram. Line $t$ crosses lines $p$ and $q$ at two different points, forming eight angles at those crossings.

Which claim correctly names the transversal and organises those angles?

options.A: Lines $p$ and $q$ are the transversal, and $t$ is only a third unrelated line.
options.B: Line $t$ is a transversal even if it meets only one of $p$ or $q$.
options.C: Line $t$ is the transversal because it meets both $p$ and $q$; the eight angles sit in vertically opposite equal pairs at each crossing.
options.D: The eight angles are what create transversal $t$ across $p$ and $q$.
